home.title: The Chess Genome
home.subtitle: Every legal position is encoded as a unique integer via the first 64 primes. We order the full space with the logarithmic function L and collaboratively build the catalogue of reachable positions.
home.how_1: Each square receives one of the first 64 primes (a1 = 2, …, h8 = 311).
home.how_2: Each piece type receives an exponent 0–12 (white pawn = 1, black king = 12, …).
home.how_3: The position is encoded as S = ∏ pᵢ^vᵢ.
home.how_4: We order with L = Σ vᵢ · log pᵢ without computing hundreds of digits.
home.how_5: The community contributes reachable positions; we build the ordered Genome.

oeis.extendedTitle: Extended FIDE encoding — b(n) = p^e (67 terms)
oeis.extendedExplain: n=1…64 squares; n=65 side to move (313^t, t=1 white / 2 black); n=66 castling (317^c); n=67 en passant (331^e). Missing right → factor 1.

blocks.content: The home page summarizes the project and shows global database statistics.
Statistics

items: Total positions: number of positions stored in MongoDB.
Admissible positions: those passing basic static checks.
Highest L₁₀ registered with associated legal game: the highest record reachable via legal FIDE moves.

blocks.content: The L₁₀ record only counts games with an associated PGN. Unreachable theoretical positions do not appear in this card.
View position / View author
The 'View position' button loads the PGN leading to that top position in the Gödelization tab, where it auto-analyzes. 'View author' shows who claimed authorship of that record position.

blocks.caption: L₁₀ record card on the home page

blocks.content: The Editor lets you build positions and play variations from any base FEN.
Play mode
Drag pieces with the mouse or click origin → target. Every move is automatically recorded in the moves panel on the right.
Edit mode

items: Select a piece from the palette and click a square to place it.
Use 🗑 to delete pieces.
'Clear' empties the board.
'Reset' returns to the starting position.

blocks.content: Paste a FEN in the input below and press Apply to load any position.
Copy PGN
The 📋 Copy PGN button copies the entire played variation with headers + base FEN. Paste it in Gödelization to analyze.
Gödelization can analyze both a single position (FEN) and complete games (PGN).
Analyze FEN

items: Paste a FEN in the blue field.
The small board shows the position live.
Press '🔍 Analyze FEN' to see L, L₁₀, S, Stockfish and neural features.

blocks.content: Analyze games (PGN)

items: Paste a PGN or load a .pgn file.
Press '📋 Paste' to paste from clipboard.
Press 'Analyze game' to process ply by ply.
The 'Auto-save' checkbox sends positions to MongoDB automatically.

blocks.content: With Auto-save enabled, every analyzed game feeds the database and the global PGN record.
Charts
After analysis, a chart shows the series L₁₀, L, D(k) and R(k). You can filter series, change label angles and press '📊 Refresh chart' to recapture with your configuration.
Search stored positions by FEN or board part.

Sort by L₁₀, L, timesSeen or pieceCount.

blocks.content: Charts show the evolution of genome magnitudes along a game.
Available series

items: L₁₀ (blue): log₁₀ of the Gödel number S. The main magnitude.
L (orange): natural log ln(S).
D(k) (pink): difference Lₖ − Lₖ₋₁ between consecutive plies.
R(k) (violet): ratio Sₖ / Sₖ₋₁ = exp(D(k)) = 10^(log₁₀ Sₖ − log₁₀ Sₖ₋₁).

blocks.content: Each series can be toggled with its colored button. Label angles are adjusted individually.

blocks.content: Every time a game is analyzed with Auto-save enabled, its maximum L₁₀ is stored in MongoDB's 'pgns' collection.

items: The global record is the game with the highest legally reachable L₁₀.
PGNs are deduplicated by hash (uploading the same game only increments timesSeen).
The author of the record position can claim authorship from Home.
